title: Keeper of the Hidden Treasure: Zombie Game - A Look at the Rarest Dungeon Crawl I Own
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xl-iPpFgCRM

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes what is probably the rarest board game he owns, and the most he has ever paid for one: Keeper of the Hidden Treasure: Zombie Game, published in Japan by Epoch around 1984. He says it cost about $350. The draw is the art, by an illustrator better known for military books in the Osprey mould, and Daniel calls it possibly the best he has seen in any dungeon crawl. The box lid becomes levels one and two, the inner box flips over for levels three and four, and a paper castle stands at the far end with a door that closes on a countdown once the first player escapes.

The game underneath is very simple. You spin to move, draw monsters at room thresholds, flip combat cards to see how much damage you deal, and collect treasure. Sealed rooms hide an empty passage, an anaconda, or a dragon that takes all your loot. Its best idea is the zombies: draw one and you spawn it, then steer it against your rivals. That was a rare twist for 1984.

Daniel's verdict is blunt. It is a serviceable family game, below TSR's Dungeon and well below DungeonQuest, and he hasn't finished a game. He admits he is half relieved, because a masterpiece nobody could buy would have been worse. With no BGG ratings and no other YouTube coverage, this may be the only look at it most people get.

----

Daniel says he was half relieved the rarest game he owns turned out not to be a hidden gem. Have you ever bought a game for its art alone, and did it earn its place on the shelf?
